| prior_art | `w3c-dwbp-2017` |
| rf_fail | For every data page looked at, the markup does not carry a date in the three fields read (dateModified, datePublished, temporalCoverage), or carries one but none of up to three recognised same-site latest-version links resolves. It is not a claim that the agency does not date or version its releases: a version number, a date in another markup field, in visible text, a PDF or a catalog record, and a latest link worded otherwise, beyond the third, or on another site are not read. |
| rf_fix_line | Publish the product's release date in the page's structured markup. |
| rf_hypothesis | Can a machine tell which release of the data it is reading, and find the latest one? An SI client that cannot read a release date may quote a superseded figure as current; one that cannot find the latest release cannot correct itself. |
| rf_not_measured | The public client could not read one or more pages, for one of three reasons: the host refused the identified client, the client's own robots.txt compliance kept it from reading the page, or a latest-version link could not be confirmed, a server or network error. |
| rf_partial | Some of the agency's data pages are dated in markup with a resolving same-site latest-version link and some are not. |
| rf_pass | Every data page looked at carried a release or modification date in its markup (in the dateModified or datePublished field, or in temporalCoverage, a case this diagnostic marks as its own choice), and a latest-version link on the same site resolved. |
| rf_plain_name | Markup dates the data; a latest-version link resolves |
| rf_question | Can a machine read which release of the data the page is showing, and follow a link to the latest release? |
| rf_requirements | [{"source": "w3c-dwbp-2017", "quote": "Assign and indicate a version number or date for each dataset."}, {"source": "w3c-dwbp-2017", "quote": "Check if a computer application can automatically detect/discover and process the unique version number or date of a dataset or distribution."}, {"source": "w3c-dwbp-2017", "quote": "Humans and software agents will be able to refer to specific versions of a dataset and to concepts such as a 'dataset series' and 'the latest version'."}, {"source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.txt", "quote": "provides a timestamp indicating the date and time at which the origin server believes the selected representation was last modified"}, {"source": "dcat-us-1-1-schema", "quote": "Most recent date on which the dataset was changed, updated or modified."}, {"source": "w3c-dwbp-2017", "quote": "Assign URIs to individual versions of datasets as well as to the overall series."}] |
| rf_rung_two_changes | Nothing: this check needs no key. |
| rf_standards_urls | https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.txt |
| rf_state | project_defined |
| rf_what_client_does | The public client asks the website for the data page, reads its date markup and header, and follows up to three same-site latest-version links to see whether they resolve. |
| rf_where_we_look | The data page itself (its structured date markup and the server's last-modified header) and up to three links on the same site that point to the latest version. |
| rf_who_else | Google Lighthouse is the nearest precedent: anyone can run its automated page-level checks against a named page and get back met, not met, or not applicable against published criteria. |
| rf_why_it_matters | A Data on the Web Best Practice asks that a machine be able to detect a dataset's version or date and refer to its latest version, and USAFacts' AI-ready data guide asks that the most recent update be retrievable by a machine; the requirement that a latest-version link actually resolve is the project's own rule. |
| rule_id | RULE-A8-v4 |
| signal | Read Last-Modified and any dcterms:modified / schema.org dateModified in the markup; test whether a latest-vintage pointer resolves. |

## Evidence

| doc_id | doc_type | title | locator (evidence cell) |
|---|---|---|---|
| dcat-us-1-1-schema | federal | DCAT-US Schema v1.1 (Project Open Data Metadata Schema) - resources.data.gov | the modified field, required "yes, always": "most recent date on which the dataset was changed, updated or modified", as an ISO 8601 date; and the accrualPeriodicity field, the publishing frequency as an ISO 8601 repeating duration |
| omb-m-23-22-digital-first-public-experience | federal | OMB M-23-22: Delivering a Digital-First Public Experience | indicate timeliness of content: agencies "should indicate when content on static, public-facing websites was created or last updated by including temporal information in line with content or by using 'Last Modified' in the HTTP header, in metadata tags, or in XML sitemaps" |
| w3c-dwbp-2017 | standard | Data on the Web Best Practices (W3C Recommendation, 31 January 2017) | BP 7, provide a version indicator: "assign and indicate a version number or date for each dataset", whose intended outcome is that "humans and software agents will easily be able to determine which version of a dataset they are working with" and whose implementation note is that "the URI used to request the latest version of the data should not change as the versions change", which is the latest-vintage pointer; and BP 21, provide data up to date: "make data available in an up-to-date manner, and make the update frequency explicit" |

Evidence cell, verbatim:

> `w3c-dwbp-2017` (BP 7, provide a version indicator: "assign and indicate a version number or date for each dataset", whose intended outcome is that "humans and software agents will easily be able to determine which version of a dataset they are working with" and whose implementation note is that "the URI used to request the latest version of the data should not change as the versions change", which is the latest-vintage pointer; and BP 21, provide data up to date: "make data available in an up-to-date manner, and make the update frequency explicit"); `dcat-us-1-1-schema` (the modified field, required "yes, always": "most recent date on which the dataset was changed, updated or modified", as an ISO 8601 date; and the accrualPeriodicity field, the publishing frequency as an ISO 8601 repeating duration); `omb-m-23-22-digital-first-public-experience` (indicate timeliness of content: agencies "should indicate when content on static, public-facing websites was created or last updated by including temporal information in line with content or by using 'Last Modified' in the HTTP header, in metadata tags, or in XML sitemaps")
